admissionBoundary.question: Is request-validation vs attempt-admission the right boundary? D9 load-bearing for C-2 identity?
admissionBoundary.answer: YES. Snapshot capture AFTER attempt-admission matches D9 analysis-snapshot-invalidated (admission=admitted, coherent-terminal-run, indeterminate, committed). The v2 invocation-vs-execution split made the same snapshot failure pre-admission in C-2 and post-admission in D9 — a hard identity fork. Making D9 load-bearing for termination identity is the correct dependency DIRECTION: termination owns identity; plan schema must not invent a second one.
admissionBoundary.dependencyDirection: C-2 → D9 (and C-2 → FACT-PLANE for relations). VERSIONING → D9 already declared. Do not reverse.

supervisedImplementationEffect.question: Real class or a licence?
supervisedImplementationEffect.answer: Real CLASS for schema and Coverage/failure semantics: scanners and semantic providers are not probes (scenario subject) and not pure rules. Representable as fact-derivation under grants. ENFORCEMENT is conditional: PS-12c / runtime denial needs ARCH.PROBE-CONTRACT (REOPENED). The CONDITIONAL discharge on 'effectful work is unrepresentable as a Rule' is correct, not defeatist — schema rejection (PS-12a/b) is real; runtime authority denial is not yet. Calling the class a licence would be accurate only if the property were marked DISCHARGED; it is not.

partialConditionalDowngrades.question: Are PARTIAL/CONDITIONAL sealed-property downgrades correct?
partialConditionalDowngrades.answer: YES. physical storage schema stays private → PARTIAL (PS-02 only; PS-07 unbuilt). effectful unrepresentable as Rule → CONDITIONAL (schema yes, runtime no). C3X blocking paper seals is the right instrument. This is honesty, not defeatism.

findings.title: supervised-implementation-effect is unenforceable at runtime until PROBE-CONTRACT
findings.evidence: effectTaxonomy.whatCCannotClose and dischargeStatus CONDITIONAL explicitly depend on ARCH.PROBE-CONTRACT REOPENED. PS-09, PS-12c implementable:false.
findings.impact: A mislabelled stage can claim fact-derivation and exercise host effects if linked TCB ignores labels. Week-one build can ship schema validation; must not claim capability confinement.
findings.requiredChange: No C-2 text change required. Build plan must treat PROBE-CONTRACT as a blocking dependency for any claim of effect confinement. Do not re-upgrade CONDITIONAL to DISCHARGED without implementable tests.
findings.whatWouldChangeMyMind: A sealed capability substrate with LN-12-class runtime denial tests implementable:true.

findings.title: Well-formed plans can be semantically absurd
findings.evidence: knownLimitations: schemas validate SHAPE; a rule depending on an unrelated derived relation is accepted.
findings.impact: Plan validation is necessary not sufficient for sound analysis graphs.
findings.requiredChange: Future work: optional semantic plan lint (depends-on vs relation dependency closure) — out of C-2 v3 seal scope if documented.
findings.whatWouldChangeMyMind: A conformance test that rejects cross-relation nonsensical dependsOn graphs.

findings.title: subjectScopeCommitment computation not owned here
findings.evidence: Coverage key requires the field; computation/verification owned by evidence/retention (REOPENED).
findings.impact: Negative-query fixtures are shape-true only until commitment verification exists.
findings.requiredChange: Cross-surface seal dependency on EVIDENCE — already knownLimitation.
findings.whatWouldChangeMyMind: EVIDENCE seals commitment algorithm with C-2 cross-check.

sealRecommendation.note: R1-C2-01 is a dependency residual already correctly marked CONDITIONAL/NOT implementable — not a defect in the contract text. R1-C2-02/03 are documented knownLimitations. Blind fixtures 18/18 match. Admission boundary and effect taxonomy are right.
sealRecommendation.caveat: SEAL the schema contract; do not seal the runtime-confinement *product claim*.
